newsitem.title: USA: Sun reports big earnings jump, stock gains.
newsitem.headline: Sun reports big earnings jump, stock gains.

text.p: Sun Co. Inc. surprised Wall Street when it reported its earnings more than doubled for the second quarter, driving the oil refiner's stock price up by more than 5 percent Thursday.
Philadelphia-based Sun said Wednesday that operating income surged to $105 million, from $50 million a year ago. The

results blew past analysts' forecasts by nearly 40 percent, according to figures published by First Call, and drove Sun stock up by $1.875 to $33 a share in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Last November, Sun appointed Jack Drosdick, formerly chief executive at Ultramar Diamond Shamrock Corp., as its new president. Analysts said the benefits of the management change are now filtering through to the bottom line, despite a 45-cent-per-barrel decline in refining margins.
"The company is way ahead on its cost cutting and achieved this result with no help from margins," said Oppenheimer analyst Bruce Lanni. "The bottom line is that we are now looking at a new company."
The sharp rise in earnings prompted Lanni to raise his 1997 earnings per share estimate to $2.55 from $2.13, and to increase his target price for the stock to $38.
With its refineries running at full tilt, Sun's Northeast refining, marketing and chemicals division earnings jumped $54 million, to $76 million.
"On the cost side, cash refinery expenses were lower by $25 million and total unit expenses were reduced by $35 million," Sun's Drosdick said.

Sun's net income totalled $105 million, compared with a loss of $3 million in the same year-ago period. The loss in last year's second quarter reflected an after-tax charge of $53 million related to the reconfiguration at its Philadelphia refinery.
Sun also said Thursday that it would buy back $150 million worth of its shares.
Another oil refining company, Tosco Corp., reported earnings that were largely in line with Wall Street expectations.

Tosco, the largest independent oil refiner in the United States, said its net income rose by 35 percent in the second quarter to $67.1 million, compared with net income of $49.6 million a year ago. Sales rose to $3.2 billion, from $2.4 billion in the same quarter a year ago.
Earnings per share were 43 cents, matching industry analysts' forecasts and up from 41 cents a share a year ago.
The sharp rise in net income was largely due to its purchase of 2,500 convenience stores from Circle K Corp in May 1996, the company said.
Tosco said that earnings were hurt weak refining margins on the West Coast.
"Tosco's second-quarter results were impacted by the dramatic decline in West Coast refining margins during May and June," said company Chairman Thomas O'Malley.
"Margins on the East Coast ... were good throughout most of the period. Retail margins were also good during the quarter in all of Tosco's marketing areas," he added.
The company also said startup expenses at its Trainer, Pa., refinery had reduced earnings by $12 million so far this year.
Tosco's stock fell 31 cents to $29.69 a share, also on the NYSE.
